name: Support tickets: class rules, never extract and a closing rule
text: Hi, after updating Fleetview to version 4.12.3 on 3 March, our Pro account was billed twice for order #A-20931 (2 x $49.00) and the app shows ERR_PAYMENT_DUPLICATE. Plan B in our rollout plan was to use the Fleetview web app instead, but it fails too. The invoice #C-48120 for the Team plan never arrived, refund reference RF-7781 hasn't shown up, and invoice INV-2026-0412 still says unpaid.
rules:
[RULES]
G1 Extract every entity of the supplied types from a customer support ticket. Return exact spans from the text.

[TYPE] PRODUCT
[DESCRIPTION] A named product or app.

[TYPE] VERSION
[DESCRIPTION] A software version number.

[TYPE] PLAN
[DESCRIPTION] A subscription plan or tier.
PL1 Label the plan name only, without the word "plan", "account" or "tier": "Business" in "our Business account".

[TYPE] ORDER_ID
[DESCRIPTION] An order number.
OI1 The span starts at the # and leaves out the word "order": "#B-11872" in "order #B-11872".

[TYPE] INVOICE_ID
[DESCRIPTION] An invoice number.

[TYPE] REFUND_REF
[DESCRIPTION] A refund reference.

[TYPE] ERROR_CODE
[DESCRIPTION] An error code shown by the product.

[TYPE] AMOUNT
[DESCRIPTION] A sum of money with its currency.

[TYPE] DATE
[DESCRIPTION] A calendar date.

[TYPE] NOT_AN_ENTITY
NE1 A "Plan" followed by a letter is a fallback strategy, never PLAN: "Plan A", "Plan C", "Plan D".
NE2 The word plan in "backup plan" or "migration plan".

[RULES]
G2 The format decides, whatever the customer calls it: a reference that starts with INV- is INVOICE_ID ("INV-2025-0099"), even when the customer calls it an order; a reference that starts with # is ORDER_ID ("#B-11872"), even when the customer calls it an invoice. This overrides everything above.
caption: A support-ticket rulebook written for this demo, not a benchmark. It uses all three kinds of rules. Class rule: the PLAN card labels "Pro", not "Pro account". Never extract: "Plan B" is a fallback, not a subscription plan. Closing rule: the reference format decides, so "#C-48120" is an order number even though the customer calls it an invoice. Delete any of them and Run to see the difference.

name: Job application: what counts as a skill
text: Priya Raman is a senior data engineer with 7 years of experience, most recently at Shopify in Toronto. She started as a Power BI developer at Deloitte. She holds an MSc in Computer Science from the University of Waterloo, works daily in Python, SQL and Spark, and speaks Spanish and Tamil.
rules:
[RULES]
G1 Extract every entity of the supplied types from a job application. Return exact spans from the text.

[TYPE] PERSON
[DESCRIPTION] The candidate's name.

[TYPE] JOB_TITLE
[DESCRIPTION] A job title the candidate has held or applies for.

[TYPE] COMPANY
[DESCRIPTION] A company the candidate has worked for.

[TYPE] DEGREE
[DESCRIPTION] A degree or diploma.

[TYPE] SCHOOL
[DESCRIPTION] A university, college or school.

[TYPE] SKILL
[DESCRIPTION] A technical skill, tool, language or platform.

[TYPE] CERTIFICATION
[DESCRIPTION] A professional certification.

[TYPE] EXPERIENCE
[DESCRIPTION] A length of work experience.
E1 Label the number with its unit: "3 years", "18 months".

[TYPE] NOT_AN_ENTITY
NE1 Spoken languages, such as "French", "Hindi" or "Mandarin".

[RULES]
G2 A job title named after a tool is JOB_TITLE as a whole, never SKILL: "SAP consultant", "Tableau developer". This overrides everything above.
caption: A job-application rulebook written for this demo, not a benchmark. Class rule: EXPERIENCE labels "7 years", not "7 years of experience". Never extract: spoken languages are not skills, so Spanish and Tamil are left out. Closing rule: a job title named after a tool stays one JOB_TITLE, so "Power BI developer" does not lose "Power BI" to SKILL. Delete any of them and Run to see the difference.

name: Clinical note: skip conditions the patient doesn't have
text: 58-year-old man seen for chest pain on exertion. History of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Denies shortness of breath; no history of stroke. Currently taking metformin 500 mg twice daily and lisinopril 10 mg once daily. Allergic to penicillin. Started atorvastatin 20 mg at night.
rules:
[RULES]
G1 Extract every entity of the supplied types from a clinical note. Return exact spans from the text.

[TYPE] CONDITION
[DESCRIPTION] A disease, symptom or diagnosis the patient has.

[TYPE] MEDICATION
[DESCRIPTION] A drug the patient takes or is prescribed.
M1 Drug name only; dose and frequency are separate.

[TYPE] DOSE
[DESCRIPTION] An amount of a drug, such as 250 mg.

[TYPE] FREQUENCY
[DESCRIPTION] How often a drug is taken, such as three times a day.
F1 Times of day count as frequency: "in the morning", "at bedtime".

[TYPE] ALLERGY
[DESCRIPTION] A substance the patient is allergic to.

[TYPE] NOT_AN_ENTITY
NE1 Conditions the patient does not have: a condition after "denies", "no", "no history of" or "negative for" ("denies fever", "no rash").

[RULES]
G2 A drug the patient is allergic to is ALLERGY, never MEDICATION ("allergic to sulfa"). This overrides everything above.
caption: A clinical-note rulebook written for this demo, not a benchmark, and not for clinical use. Never extract: conditions the patient does not have, so "shortness of breath" and "stroke" are left out. Class rule: times of day count as FREQUENCY, so "at night" is found. Delete either of them and Run to see the difference.
